viewsWelcome.contents:
No ERD domains found.

ERD Studio lets you design your data warehouse visually across two stages:

**Logical** — columns, data types, FK keys, and design rationale
**Physical** — read-only view of what's built in dbt

[Set Up ERD Studio](command:erdStudio.setupSemanticDirectory)

Creates the .erd-studio directory structure and your first domain.

[Install AI Coding Harness](command:erdStudio.installCodingHarness)

Add ERD Studio schema reference to Claude, Copilot, Gemini, or Codex.

No logical models found.

Models are stored as YAML files in .erd-studio/logical-models/.

Add models to a domain using the ERD editor to create them here.

erdStudio.claudeSync.skipPermissions.markdownDescription: When **Execute with Claude** launches Claude Code to apply a sync plan, pass `--dangerously-skip-permissions` so it edits files without asking. Off by default: Claude Code prompts before each file change. The launch command is always shown for confirmation first.

erdStudio.feedback.aiAssist.markdownDescription: Let the Feedback dialog make **one** request to a language model to draft a title, pick bug vs feature, and check for duplicate issues. Only what you typed is sent — diagnostics, file paths and model names never are. Your own model is used where VS Code has one (VS Code asks for access itself, once); otherwise `#erdStudio.feedback.endpoint#`, or — if `#erdStudio.feedback.hostedFallback#` is on — a relay run by the extension author that forwards your description to a named third-party AI provider under the author's account. That last one always asks first and names both. Turn this off to make no request at all.

markdownEnumDescriptions: Your editor's language model first, then `#erdStudio.feedback.endpoint#`, then the ERD Studio service. The old default; still honoured, no longer offered in the dialog.
Only your editor's own language model. Nothing is sent anywhere else; if this editor has none, the Feedback dialog simply shows no analysis.
Only `#erdStudio.feedback.endpoint#`, with the key you stored via **ERD Studio: Set Feedback API Key**. Not offered in the dialog unless you have already picked it here.

Only the small relay run by the extension author, which forwards your description to a third-party AI provider under the author's account. Pick this if you have Copilot but would rather not spend it on triaging feedback. Requires `#erdStudio.feedback.hostedFallback#` to be on, and asks before the first request.
erdStudio.feedback.provider.markdownDescription: Which model triages your feedback. The Feedback dialog offers two: your editor’s own model, or the ERD Studio service. Each pins one destination and does **not** fall through — if the one you pick is unavailable here, the dialog says so and offers the other rather than quietly sending your text somewhere you did not choose. `auto` (the old default, your own model first) and `endpoint` still work if you set them here, but the dialog no longer offers them.

erdStudio.feedback.hostedFallback.markdownDescription: As a last resort — when VS Code offers no language model and `#erdStudio.feedback.endpoint#` is empty — allow the Feedback dialog to send your description to a small relay run by the extension author, which forwards it to a third-party AI provider under the author's account and that provider's terms. You are always asked first — the prompt names the relay and the provider — and the request carries only what you typed. Turn this off to keep feedback analysis on your own model or endpoint only.

erdStudio.feedback.endpoint.markdownDescription: Base URL of an OpenAI-compatible chat-completions API for feedback analysis (e.g. `https://api.openai.com/v1`). Leave empty to use VS Code's built-in language model when one is available. The API key is stored in secret storage via **ERD Studio: Set Feedback API Key**, never in settings.

erdStudio.feedback.trackReports.markdownDescription: Show a **My Reports** view listing issues you filed from ERD Studio, refreshed from GitHub every few hours. Requires you to be signed in to GitHub in VS Code; the view is hidden otherwise and you are never prompted to sign in.
